key_insight: This paper introduces TACT, a training approach that helps language agents achieve social goals while saying less. The main idea is to make agents communicate more efficiently without sacrificing negotiation or coordination quality.
problem_solved: It tackles the challenge of socially intelligent language agents being too verbose during negotiation and coordination. The goal is to reduce communication cost while still handling conflicting preferences and respecting the time and attention of both participants.
method: Teacher-Assisted Communication Training (TACT) uses teacher guidance to shape better communication behavior during training.
The method encourages agents to share only the information needed to advance the interaction and satisfy partner constraints.
It balances task success with brevity, aiming to improve social goal attainment while minimizing unnecessary words.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means building agents that are more practical, cheaper to use, and better suited for real interactive settings. Efficient communication is especially valuable in multi-agent systems, customer support, and negotiation-style applications.

paper_title: Towards Communication-Efficient Social Intelligence in Language Agents
paper_authors: Linxiao Gong, Yijie Xu, Tianfu Wang, Yin Wu, Yili Wang
